input.quote: This Agreement and the performance of transactions under this Agreement shall be governed by the substantive laws of the state of New York.
input.rationale:
Section 16.9 selects New York substantive law and requires any action to be commenced "in a court sited within the State of New York," i.e. litigation in New York courts rather than arbitration. No arbitration provision exists anywhere in the document, and the ancillary general clauses (CI Agreement § 8 at p1499 and Loan Agreement § 16 at p1587) both also choose New York law, so there is no conflicting law or venue choice. This meets the preferred position (New York law, New York courts). Noted only as a minor point short of the preferred wording: venue is not expressly stated to be the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, and the clause adds a contractual limitations period — neither is a material deviation and neither is flagged.</parationale>
